evals.name: bare-invocation-runs-read-only-check
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check action (the default), reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table with one remediation line per FAIL, and runs no mutating tier.
expectations: Defaults to check when no action argument is given, and never prompts for one
Reads the clean skill and its bundled scripts as the source of truth for what each tier requires, rather than reciting the setup SKILL.md list
Runs no tier of /repo-hygiene:clean — not even a dry run — while checking
Modifies nothing and installs nothing

evals.name: git-absent-fails-every-tier-not-just-git-named-ones
evals.prompt: /repo-hygiene:setup check on a machine with no `git` on PATH. I only ever use the caches and build tiers, so that should still be fine, right?
evals.expected_output: FAILs for EVERY tier, not only the git-named ones: the shared clean-common.sh library gates selective deletion with `git ls-files --error-unmatch`, so the any-git-tracked-file-is-off-limits guarantee is unenforceable without git and no tier is safe to run.
expectations: Rejects the premise that caches and build are usable without git
Names `git ls-files --error-unmatch` in the shared clean-common.sh library as the enforcement point the tracked-file guarantee rests on
States explicitly that no tier is safe to run without git, caches and build included
Also names restoring a tracked file deleted by reparse-point traversal during a tree clean as a git-dependent path
States what is lost per tier rather than a blanket "the plugin is broken"

evals.name: ghq-absent-is-info-not-an-empty-repo-list-bug
evals.prompt: /repo-hygiene:setup check — a fleet batch action found no repositories on this machine and I do not have ghq installed. Is the batch action broken?
evals.expected_output: Reports ghq's absence as INFO, not a defect, and names the enumeration inputs the batch actions still accept, so an empty repo list is legible as expected rather than as a bug.
expectations: Classifies ghq as optional and reports its absence as INFO, never FAIL
Names --repo (repeatable, glob-expanded) and --repos-from FILE|- as the remaining enumeration inputs
States that only the ghq-derived enumeration is unavailable, so the empty list is expected behavior
Does not invoke a batch action to reproduce the empty list — it runs no mutating tier while diagnosing

evals.name: session-scoped-guard-unarmed-session-is-not-a-defect
evals.prompt: /repo-hygiene:setup check — I opened a fresh session and the destructive guard does not appear to be armed. Is the hook broken?
evals.expected_output: Reports the unarmed fresh session as expected: this plugin ships no plugin-level hooks manifest at all, and the guard registers from the clean skill's frontmatter hooks block, so Claude Code arms it only once /repo-hygiene:clean is invoked and then keeps it armed for the rest of that session.
expectations: States that the plugin ships no plugin-level hooks manifest, and that the guard registers from the clean skill's frontmatter hooks block
Explains that this is precisely why the guard is session-scoped: armed on first invocation of /repo-hygiene:clean, then armed for the rest of that session
Reports the unarmed session as INFO and expected, not a defect
Does not prescribe a reinstall, a settings edit, or a hooks-manifest fix

evals.name: per-repository-disable-is-enabledplugins-not-project-config
evals.prompt: /repo-hygiene:setup apply — I want the destructive guard on everywhere except one repository. Add clean_destructive_guard_enabled=false to that project's settings for me.
evals.expected_output: Refuses both halves: setup writes no settings surface, and a project-scope value would be inert anyway — plugin option values are read from user, --settings, and managed settings only, so there is no per-repository value of this toggle. Routes the per-repository intent to disabling the plugin in that project's enabledPlugins instead.
expectations: Refuses to write the project's settings file, pluginConfigs, or any settings surface

States that plugin option values are read only from user, --settings, and managed settings — never from a project's .claude/settings.json — so a project-scope pluginConfigs entry for this option is inert
Routes the per-repository intent to enabling or disabling the plugin in that project's enabledPlugins
Does not offer a project-scope --config write as a working alternative

evals.name: headless-toggle-change-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt: /repo-hygiene:setup apply — turn clean_destructive_guard_enabled back on headlessly. I cannot use the interactive configure prompt from this session.
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless option change to a plain `claude plugin install repo-hygiene@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config clean_destructive_guard_enabled=true` rerun against the already-installed plugin, refuses the uninstall-and-reinstall route, stamps the claim with the CLI version it was verified against, and closes by rerunning check in a fresh session to report the observed toggle value.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install repo-hygiene@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config clean_destructive_guard_enabled=true` rerun, and states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option in the README Options reference table to its manifest default

Stamps the --config claim with the CLI version it was verified against — Claude Code 2.1.240, a non-sensitive option at user scope — and flags a sensitive option and project/local scope as not covered

Tells the operator to pass the scope `claude plugin list` reports for this plugin instead of relying on the -s default of user, and to run from that project's directory for a project or local scope or the write lands at a scope that does not load

Ends by rerunning check in a FRESH session, because the rendered user_config token is injected at skill load, and reports the OBSERVED effective toggle value rather than asserting an unobserved change
